item.title: Looking back on who I was and where I am now
item.description:
I did these Zeigfeld style pics some years ago after having surgeries when my confidence was so low... I was so lost and scared back then but eventually that young woman found some way to her own little world of freedom with her own car, her own place, and a job with nice people...
I can see the timidness, the fear and uncertainty just from that small glimpse of my half turned face here... but how did I get here now, back to feeling so lost and scared. I was scared and lonely back then, and even worse now. That's one thing that will always tear me apart is that the man I thought was my angel, my safety and salvation, and path to a better life turned out to be the worst thing to ever happen to me and destroy me more than anything or anyonr ever has. And he still can't grasp that. He doesn't think all he's done and lied about is that bad. I know many are annoyed how much I bitch and complain about my husband, but trauma and grieving fucks you up in such horrific ways no one understand unless they have been through it too. I wish I could be that young lady who was finding her path, had her struggles then too but not like this. I want to glow again. I want to one day be so alone and independant of anyone because no one has ever made me happier than I can make myself. Anyway, just reflecting on how fast time went by and ranting as usual. I applied for more jobs today. Cross fingers I get responded to.

item.title: GovBrief Today #574
item.description: Twenty masked federal agents held off a tribe's police so contractors could start drilling for Donald Trump's border wall. They came onto the Tohono O'odham Nation in Arizona at four in the morning Tuesday with a Border Patrol SWAT team and drill trucks to work three sites. The Nation had posted No Trespassing signs two weeks earlier. The agents parked their vehicles across the road when tribal police arrived to remove the contractors. The federal government has owned a 60-foot strip along the border for 119 years, and a judge ruled two weeks ago that the wall can stand on it. Getting there means crossing the Nation's lands, and the Nation told the government to stay out. The government ignored the warning and showed up with a SWAT team. item.title: I made a Baby Book for Moms! [OC]
item.description:
I made the book I wished I had when I was a new mom to a very angry baby. Being a new mom is hard. When your baby is angry, it can feel even harder. I made this little board book to offer a few smiles and a mental hug to those moms who are in the thick of it. It will not be like this forever. And you are a good mama.
There's more pages of Vincent being hilariously mad at stuff before the ending hits, but I thought it was important to show how it ends because that's the hug I want to give! -Oh and the pancake and lollipop ones shown here actually happened!

item.title: A simple couple with an extraordinary legacy.
item.description: Du Yingrong and Lu Suying, a childless couple from Shanghai, lived an extraordinarily frugal life to help others. Living in a tiny apartment with second-hand furniture, they frequently split a single $2.50 canteen meal and mended their glasses with adhesive tape. Behind their quiet lifestyle was immense generosity. Over decades, they quietly donated their lifetime savings of 5 million yuan ($735,000 USD) to charity. Their selfless contributions paid for life-saving heart operations for 455 children suffering from congenital heart defects, leaving behind a profound legacy of quiet devotion and human kindness.
